test.name: Multiple warnings on one person escalate to identity-confusion review
test.description: User asks to check Patrick. The tool returns four warnings: three on Patrick himself (hasEventAfterDeath1 contradiction + hasAgeRangeGreaterThan120 contradiction + tooManyDeathDates2 implausible) and one on his relative Thomas (relativesHasAgeRangeGreaterThan120 contradiction). Per the cluster-escalation rule in warnings-as-identity-signals.md, '2+ contradictions on one person -> almost certainly two people merged.' The skill should NOT just list four warnings independently. It should explicitly recognize the cluster (2 contradictions + 1 implausible ON PATRICK, not counting Thomas's separate relative warning) as a strong identity-confusion signal, separate Thomas's warning into its own treatment, and recommend a timeline review + person_evidence rebuild for Patrick.

input.user_message: Run a thorough warnings check on Patrick Flynn.

judge_context: Should call person_warnings on Patrick (I1) and report all four warnings the tool returned

Should explicitly recognize the cluster of warnings ON PATRICK (2 contradictions + 1 implausible on I1) as a cluster rather than four independent items -- and should first ask whether ONE wrong fact would produce the whole cluster before treating it as identity confusion. All three of Patrick's warnings cite the same death fact, so a single wrong death date is a live explanation standing alongside a merge, not a lesser one.

Should count ONLY Patrick's three warnings toward the cluster verdict, NOT the fourth warning which is on his relative Thomas (I2) -- relativesHasAgeRangeGreaterThan120 is a separate concern about the parent-child link, not another strike against Patrick
Should treat Thomas's relative-warning per the relative-warning rule: recommend verifying the parent-child link via person-evidence BEFORE recommending data fixes on Thomas

Should recommend verifying the shared fact -- the recorded death date -- against its original source as the FIRST move, since that one check distinguishes a data-entry error from an identity problem. Recommending a chronological timeline rebuild, and re-linking the assertions once a split is actually established, is correct as the follow-on rather than the opening move. Phrase both as research actions the user can take: naming an internal skill in user-facing text is itself a defect under the skill's phrasing rule.
Should classify the severities correctly: hasEventAfterDeath1, hasAgeRangeGreaterThan120, and relativesHasAgeRangeGreaterThan120 as Critical (contradiction); tooManyDeathDates2 as Note (implausible)

Should not present a single field fix as resolving the cluster on its own. Recommending that the shared death date be verified first is correct and expected -- it is the discriminator -- but the report must keep the identity reading open until that check is done, rather than closing on either explanation.

Should reflect the escalation rule from warnings-as-identity-signals.md as it now stands: on 2+ contradictions, ask first whether one wrong fact explains all of them, and treat the merge reading as the stronger one only when no single error does.
